candidates.decision_relevance: A matched, time-ordered breadth history would help distinguish persistent participation deterioration from a transient endpoint or changing proxy membership, a recurring uncertainty in the distribution-versus-rebound analyses.
candidates.evidence_reference: Weekly reviews W37–W42 and daily reviews 2026-10-23–24 describe missing breadth sequences, non-comparable membership hashes, or proxy-only snapshots.
candidates.metric_name: Constituent-level breadth history with point-in-time universe membership
candidates.missing_history_problem: The supplied breadth evidence is mostly point-in-time counts or rolling summaries, often with changing constituents and unclear ordering against price moves. Historical constituent membership and returns would permit consistent, reproducible breadth series and temporal comparisons.

candidates.decision_relevance: A multi-session settled-flow history would clarify whether isolated mixed or negative ETF observations were persistent and how flows evolved alongside price and participation, without treating a single session as a trend.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily reviews repeatedly cite only the latest settled ETF session; weekly reviews note missing numerical totals or time-ordered flow observations.
candidates.metric_name: Settled BTC and ETH ETF net flows by session
candidates.missing_history_problem: The analyses lack a consistently supplied, time-ordered series of settled daily flows for both assets. Single-session values cannot show persistence, reversals, or alignment with the observed price and breadth paths.
